body.statement:
There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed constants of \(\mathcal M\), such that the corrected two-tolerance certified algorithm terminates for every sample and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), returns a finite collection \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) satisfying
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\subseteq\{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n\}\subseteq\{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le C\epsilon_n^2\}.
\]
Every retained box has \(\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\ne\varnothing\), and, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a),\qquad \operatorname{rad}J_{b,n}(a)\le\zeta_n.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 0\le\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\le C\left[\left\{\frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}\right\}^{\beta-1/2}+\zeta_n\right]\le Cr_n
\]
uniformly over \(a\in I\). Writing \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\), the certificate count obeys
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\left\{C\left(K_n^2+\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\right)\log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
In the simpler regime \(\beta>3/2\), this becomes
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\left\{CK_n^2\log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
body.justification: Honesty is operational only if every exact-profile law is enclosed, every endpoint box has a decoded feasible witness, and every represented law remains in a controlled enlarged profile.
body.gap: Existing finite-frequency inversions do not establish a continuum law-valued discrepancy sandwich with separate constraint and endpoint tolerances.
body.consumer: Users receive finite outward endpoints whose full diameter, rather than an unsupported distance to exact extrema, is certified at the statistical inverse-modulus scale.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\gamma=\beta-1/2\), which is positive by the corrected domain \(\beta>1/2\).  Fix the realized sample throughout this proof.  For a candidate \(Q\in\mathcal M\), collect its probability channels, its marked channels divided by \(B_Y\), and its stratum masses in the Hilbert direct sum
\[
 \mathbb H=
 \bigoplus_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \{L^2(\mathcal C_*)\oplus L^2(\mathcal C_*)\oplus\mathbb R\},
 \qquad
 Z_Q=\bigl(F_{x,Q},B_Y^{-1}G_{x,Q},p_{x,Q}\bigr)_{x\in\mathcal X}.
\]
If \(\widehat Z_n\) denotes the analogous empirical vector, the definition of the continuous profile gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathscr D_n(Q)=\|Z_Q-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}^2. \tag{1}
\]

We first verify that the subdivisions prescribed by the corrected certificate definition are finite.  Let \(h\) be supported on \(\mathcal A=[-B_A,B_A]\) and satisfy \(\|h\|_{H^\beta}\le R\).  With \(h_T\) denoting the inverse Fourier integral restricted to \(|t|\le T\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|h-h_T\|_\infty
 \le \frac{R}{2\pi}
 \left\{\int_{|t|>T}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le C R T^{1/2-\beta}=C R T^{-\gamma}. \tag{2}
\]
The integral in (2) is finite precisely because \(\beta>1/2\).  To count a net without discretizing an inverse problem, embed \([-B_A,B_A]\) in the larger interval \([-2B_A,2B_A]\) and periodically extend \(h\) there.  Because \(h\) vanishes off \([-B_A,B_A]\), this extension has Fourier coefficients \((c_\ell)_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}(1+\ell^2)^\beta|c_\ell|^2\le C R^2. \tag{3a}
\]
For its partial Fourier sum \(S_Jh\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|h-S_Jh\|_\infty
 \le \sum_{|\ell|>J}|c_\ell|
 \le C R\left\{\sum_{\ell>J}\ell^{-2\beta}\right\}^{1/2}
 \le C R J^{-\gamma}. \tag{3b}
\]
Choose \(J\asymp u^{-1/\gamma}\) and round each of the \(2J+1\) complex coefficients outward on a grid of mesh \(u/(8J+4)\).  The rounding error in sup norm is at most \(u/2\), while (3b) bounds the truncation error by \(u/2\).  Since every coefficient has modulus at most \(CR\), this supplies a uniform \(u\)-net with at most
\[
 \exp\{C u^{-1/\gamma}\log(C/u)\} \tag{3}
\]
elements.  Applying this construction to each \(f_{x,Q}\) and \(q_{x,Q}\) is legitimate by the density and marked-density Sobolev assumptions.  Because \(f_{x,Q}(a)\ge\kappa>0\) on \(I\), interval division is continuous there and preserves outward inclusion.  The finite-stratum map
\[
 (p,f,q)\longmapsto \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x/f_x \tag{4}
\]
therefore has a finite outward cover of radius \(u\), after changing only a constant depending on \(\kappa\), \(|\mathcal X|\), \(R_f\), \(R_q\), and \(B_Y\).  Explicitly, Sobolev embedding as proved by the same Cauchy--Schwarz calculation at \(T=0\) gives \(\|q_x\|_\infty\le C R_q\), and for denominators \(f,f'\ge\kappa\),
\[
 \left|\frac{q}{f}-\frac{q'}{f'}\right|
 \le \kappa^{-1}|q-q'|+\kappa^{-2}|q'|\,|f-f'|. \tag{4a}
\]
Together with \(0\le p_x\le1\) and the finiteness of \(\mathcal X\), (4a) proves the asserted continuity and the claimed outward-cover radius.

For the error coordinates, the second-moment assumption yields, for every \(T>0\),
\[
 Q(|U_j|>T)\le M_eT^{-2},
 \qquad
 |E_Qe^{isU_j}-E_Qe^{itU_j}|
 \le |s-t|E_Q|U_j|\le \sqrt{M_e}|s-t|. \tag{5}
\]
Thus truncation produces an outward tail disk and the remaining transform is uniformly continuous on the compact protected frequency interval.  The corrected certificate keeps the exact discrepancy and the analytic and tail remainders as outward interval coordinates; it does not replace a tail remainder by zero.  For the normalized truncated law, its vector of monomials through order \(2K_n\) belongs to the convex hull of the compact moment curve: otherwise a separating linear functional would be strictly larger at the barycenter than at every point being averaged, a contradiction.  Hence it has a finite convex representation.  Whenever that representation uses more than \(2K_n+2\) positive weights, affine dependence of the corresponding moment vectors permits a signed perturbation of the weights that preserves every recorded moment and makes at least one weight zero.  Iteration gives a positive atomic quadrature exact through order \(2K_n\); multiplying its weights by the truncated mass restores the original subprobability moments.  Taylor remainder intervals, the tail disk in (5), and outward complex interval arithmetic then cover the exact channel coordinates.  The order-\(K_n\) paired-channel description has at most \(C K_n^2\) coefficient, quadrature, tail, constraint, and analytic-remainder coordinates.  The endpoint cover from (3), used with \(u=\zeta_n\), requires at most \(C\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\) further coordinates.  All coordinate ranges are compact after the moment truncation; their radii grow at most polynomially in \(K_n\), \(\tau_n^{-1}\), and \(\zeta_n^{-1}\).  Consequently, dyadic outward subdivision to constraint radius \(\tau_n\) and endpoint radius \(\zeta_n\) stops after finitely many cuts and gives
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|
 \le
 \exp\left\{C\left(K_n^2+\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\right)
 \log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}. \tag{6}
\]
This also proves termination for every realized sample, because empirical channel values are bounded and continuous on \(\mathcal C_*\), while all comparisons and interval operations use deterministic outward rounding.

We next establish the two set inclusions that repair maximality.  Write \([d_b^-,d_b^+]\) for the outward interval enclosing \(\mathscr D_n(Q)\) for decoded laws in a terminal box \(b\).  Its radius is at most \(\tau_n\), hence its length is at most \(2\tau_n\).  A box is retained only if \(d_b^-\le\epsilon_n^2\), and empty decoded boxes are excluded.  Every \(Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) is contained in an outward box, and the box containing it satisfies
\[
 d_b^-\le \mathscr D_n(Q)\le\epsilon_n^2;
\]
it is therefore retained.  This proves \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\).  Conversely, if \(Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\) for a retained box, then
\[
 \mathscr D_n(Q)\le d_b^+\le d_b^-+2\tau_n
 \le\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n. \tag{7}
\]
The corrected definition sets \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\), so (7) also gives \(\mathscr D_n(Q)\le3\epsilon_n^2\).  Since every decoder admits only members of \(\mathcal M\), (7) proves the complete discrepancy sandwich in the statement.

For endpoint validity, fix a retained \(b\) and \(a\in I\).  Every decoded law is in \(\mathcal M\), so its density denominator is at least \(\kappa\) on \(I\).  Hence intersecting the denominator enclosure with \([\kappa,\infty)\) retains every exact denominator and makes interval division valid.  Inclusion isotonicity of outward interval addition, multiplication, and division applied to (4) proves
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a). \tag{8}
\]
The endpoint stopping rule gives \(\operatorname{rad}J_{b,n}(a)\le\zeta_n\).  Notice that no comparison with an endpoint of the exact profile has been used.

It remains to control the diameter of the certified endpoint profile.  Because the retained collection is finite and each decoded set is nonempty, for any two retained boxes \(b,c\) we may choose witnesses \(Q_b\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\) and \(Q_c\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(c)\).  From (1), (7), and the triangle inequality in \(\mathbb H\),
\[
 \|Z_{Q_b}-Z_{Q_c}\|_{\mathbb H}
 \le \|Z_{Q_b}-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}
      +\|Z_{Q_c}-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}
 \le 2\sqrt{3}\,\epsilon_n. \tag{9}
\]
For sufficiently large \(n\), the right side is in the small-discrepancy regime of the already-established paired protected inverse theorem.  That theorem and (9) imply
\[
 \sup_{b,c}\|\mu_{Q_b}-\mu_{Q_c}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le C\left\{
 \frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}
 \right\}^{\gamma}. \tag{10}
\]
Multiplying the argument of the logarithms by the fixed constant \(2\sqrt3\) changes the right side only by a fixed factor for small \(\epsilon_n\).

Let \(b_-\) attain the finite minimum defining \(\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\), and let \(b_+\) attain the finite maximum defining \(\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\).  By (8) and the radius bound,
\[
 \inf J_{b_-,n}(a)\ge \mu_{Q_{b_-}}(a)-2\zeta_n,
 \qquad
 \sup J_{b_+,n}(a)\le \mu_{Q_{b_+}}(a)+2\zeta_n. \tag{11}
\]
Subtracting in (11) and applying (10) yields, uniformly in \(a\in I\),
\[
 0\le \overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)
 \le C\left\{
 \frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}
 \right\}^{\gamma}+4\zeta_n. \tag{12}
\]
Since \(\epsilon_n=C_\alpha\sqrt{\log(en/\alpha)/n}\),
\[
 \log(1/\epsilon_n)=\tfrac12\log n+O(\log\log n),
 \qquad
 \log\log(1/\epsilon_n)=\log\log n+O(1). \tag{13}
\]
The definitions of \(K_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\zeta_n\), with fixed \(c_K>0\), therefore give
\[
 \left\{\frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}\right\}^{\gamma}
 \le C K_n^{-\gamma}=Cr_n,
 \qquad
 \zeta_n=r_n/\log(en)=o(r_n). \tag{14}
\]
Equations (12)--(14) prove the asserted endpoint-width bound.

Finally, \(\log(en)\asymp K_n\log K_n\), and therefore
\[
 \zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}
 =K_n\{\log(en)\}^{1/\gamma}
 \le C K_n^{1+1/\gamma}(\log K_n)^{1/\gamma}. \tag{15}
\]
When \(\beta>3/2\), one has \(\gamma>1\), so the last expression is at most \(C K_n^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Substitution into (6) proves the simpler \(K_n^2\) certificate-count regime and completes the proof.
